decisions.reason: The pandemic froze air travel before the app could be tested, so its value is still unresolved, and a software app costs little to maintain as aviation recovers in 2022. It is the weakest option, though, because airlines run their own apps and it overlaps with Product C.

PassBoard was formally launched as a flagship passenger-processing technology just before COVID, so its uncertainty has not resolved. It fits the firm's core airport business and costs little to keep, so keeping the option open for the 2022 travel recovery is worth more than dropping it.

Demand for self-service and contactless check-in is likely to rise as airports restart under hygiene and staffing pressures, so this option may gain value. It is relatively cheap to keep alongside the firm's integrated airport services.
